editorial: If you want a wild comic book ride, this sequel throws Johnny Blaze back into the fire. He is hiding from his curse when a monk named Moreau asks him to protect a boy named Danny and his mother Nadya. The devil, called Roarke, wants Danny as a human body so he can walk the earth and cause chaos. Johnny does not want to become Ghost Rider again, but the danger pulls him in. The movie has a dark, gritty feel, with burning skulls, fast chases, and strange humor. Nicolas Cage gives a big, loud performance that fits the crazy tone, even when the story gets messy. The action is loud and fast, and the camera work can feel shaky. Some scenes are fun, while others drag or feel confusing. If you enjoy over-the-top superhero movies, you will probably have a good time. For the best experience, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Roarke tries to put his power into Danny during a dark ritual. Johnny becomes Ghost Rider and fights through Roarke's men, including Carrigan, whose touch decays everything. Ghost Rider stops the ritual, defeats Roarke, and saves Danny and Nadya. Instead of losing the curse, Johnny chooses to keep it and use it for good. He rides away into the night, leaving Danny safe and the devil's plan ruined.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves chaotic comic book action and Nicolas Cage at his wildest.
